facts: Aleph exposes explicit provider-neutral capability identities; web.crawl is the first capability with a complete executable package pipeline.

A connector execution is represented by an ingestion run with source and connector identity, capability, parameters, lifecycle, attempts, checkpoints, stats, completeness, and structured failure state.
Landing is the complete master application schema and source of truth for shared database vocabulary; Aleph only appends prefixed operational tables.
The frontier is database-backed, breadth-first, and unique by run and canonical URL hash.
Every retrieved response must be accepted by Funes before Aleph marks its candidate fetched.
Aleph stores stable Funes observation references and first, unchanged, or changed dispositions but no response bodies.
External URLs are recorded as skipped frontier candidates and typed Funes discoveries but are never claimed for recursive retrieval.
Every retrieved observation is classified as HTML, PDF, or unsupported and receives one versioned Funes extraction outcome before its frontier candidate becomes fetched.
HTML extraction records text and link, iframe, and embed discovery relationships.
PDF response bytes remain the immutable Funes payload while aleph.pdf:1 records text from the embedded text layer.
The Waverly calendar page resolves through Funes discovery provenance to its external Google Drive PDF iframe without requesting the external resource.

The landing model-attribute ownership matrix assigns aleph/core the ingestion-run concept with id, source_reference, capability, status, parameters, stats, error, started_at, and finished_at, and funes/core the observation concept with observed_at, ingested_at, payload_hash, and byte_size; extraction facts carried onto another table use extraction_status and extraction_error.
The frontier records what the Funes boundary returned: observation reference, disposition, payload hash, byte size, ingestion time, and the versioned extraction outcome.
An inventory is a deterministic report of one ingestion run, derived on read and stored nowhere.
Every inventory row is current, stale, or unobserved, and last_observed_at says when its content evidence was taken.
AHSD runs SchoolMessenger Presence, confirmed from the captured district page footer.
AHSD calendar pages render a client-side component and carry no event data in the served HTML.
ahsd.org robots.txt disallows /Search/, /WebApi/, /WebServices/, /portal/svc/, and the StaffDirectory, WorkspaceCalendar, and CalendarPicker asmx services.
No captured working request returns SchoolMessenger calendar event data, and every path such a request would occupy is robots-disallowed.
AHSD calendar paths are readable slugs such as /our_school/calendar, not a platform module path.
One district calendar artifact on Google Drive is iframed from four allowed-host homepages, so a single external resource holds four discovery parents.
District PDFs live under /UserFiles/Servers/Server_<id>/File/ and 301 to cdnsm{n}-ss20.sharpschool.com, so their Funes identity is a CDN URL.
aleph.pdf:1 extracted 832 characters from a captured 84,401-byte AHSD PDF.
sa.ahsd.org and nr.ahsd.org are allowed by *.ahsd.org but absent from the seeds, so they enter the frontier only by discovery.
aleph_ingestion_runs.source_reference stores the prefixed web:ahsd form, byte-identical to funes_sources.reference; WebSource::reference() is the only place the prefix is written.
Neither aleph_ nor funes_ tables exist in landing's database yet, so no persisted row changes meaning.
Landing has provider-specific project, path, domain, Slack-contact, and GitHub-contributor associations but no portable source-scope relation.
Aleph source-scope associations use typed namespaced Funes references and snapshot their resolution state into accepted observation metadata.
Domain reconciliation reuses source-scope associations for explicit project, site, and repository decisions without domain-name inference.
Landing SyncRun combines repository pipeline state with subway-map presentation and stores its current step and ordered steps as JSON.
Aleph ingestion runs now preserve connector/source identity, stable legacy references, replay keys, checkpoints, completeness, failures, counters, and accepted Funes references.
A logical connector ingestion run owns numbered durable attempts and exposes a presentation-neutral inspection read model.
Landing DomainSyncRun repeats the common run lifecycle and adds account/domain scope, targets, DNS counters, and provider-account/domain foreign keys.
Landing manual ingestion entry points create provider-specific run rows and dispatch through commands, jobs, or detached processes without one universal request contract.
Funes stores Aleph envelope metadata as append-only typed assertions: aleph:envelope for universal attributes and aleph:extension/<namespace> for connector extensions.
Every queued connector unit is a durable Aleph ingestion attempt with queue class, priority, tags, dispatch policy, runtime job and worker identity, heartbeat, and retry lineage.

Checkpoint history is isolated by source stream, capability, and partition and records connector serialization, optimistic version, progression rule, committing run/attempt, and accepted-through Funes references.
Every incomplete ingestion run exposes remaining work, warning and error counts, an immutable failure timeline, and one machine-readable safe recovery action.
A retry is a numbered child attempt reconstructed from the original run's durable parameters, checkpoint, counters, and idempotent identity.
Resume reconstructs each partition from its latest accepted-through checkpoint under an expiring lease and explicit partition, record, and runtime budgets.
Every active source stream has a package freshness projection or an explicit never-synchronized read model, and freshness is recalculated against an explicit clock.
Connector health is an immutable expiring result per installation dimension, aggregated with explicit unknown evidence and coded remediation.
Recurring ingestion schedules validate connector capabilities, calculate timezone-aware next runs, use expiring distributed claims, and record every schedule occurrence against its ingestion run.
Historical backfills require formatted range bounds, deterministic partitions, explicit rate/work budgets, cumulative progress, checkpoints, and all-partitions-complete termination.
Incremental streams declare cursor, high-water, webhook, hash, or reconcile strategy; only Funes-accepted material changes advance checkpoints, while unchanged polls accept zero changes.

GitHub polling and verified webhooks submit canonical node revisions through one history identity; GraphQL cursors advance after Funes acceptance, webhook deliveries are encrypted and replayable, and delivery identity is isolated by source installation.
Repository watches retain only portable orchestration state and coalesce duplicate poll/webhook triggers; repository, commit, pull-request, and file history remains outside Aleph watch storage.
Repository poll, webhook, and reconciliation signals converge on watch/ref/head identity and launch the existing checkpointed incremental workflow; watch head state does not advance during launch.

Zsh, Atuin, and Claude Bash adapters normalize shell commands with host/user execution context; shell.secrets:1 redacts credentials before Funes acceptance and exact source-record revisions replay idempotently.
Claude, Codex, and alternate-provider adapters preserve raw message blocks and references beside neutral chronology, authorship, parent, thread, branch, sidechain, agent, and part values.

Landing LinearSyncRun rows import under deterministic identity into the shared lifecycle, with Linear workspace/project scope, provider reconciliation, targets, and cursors isolated in a typed extension.

Linear workspaces ingest independently through package-owned pagination; each resource stream has its own accepted-through cursor, while verified webhooks and polling share canonical activity identity.

Gmail, Microsoft Graph, and IMAP records normalize to provider-neutral F28 messages; bounded mailbox pages advance opaque provider checkpoints only after Funes acceptance, and attachments remain Digory references.
Slack credential migration retains workspace/account/scopes/status/timestamps and an opaque host secret-store reference; token material and legacy-row deletion remain outside Aleph.
Landing SlackSyncRun rows import into the shared lifecycle with Slack workspace/channel scope and reconciled cursor, oldest, and high-water checkpoint state.

Slack polling and verified Events API observations converge through canonical activity identity; cursor/high-water checkpoints advance after Funes acceptance and attachment chunks hand off to Digory references.
assumptions: A sequential concurrency ceiling of one is sufficient for the bounded AHSD crawl.
Configured source keys remain stable Funes source references when prefixed with web:.
The configured query-parameter allowlist defines URL identity for each web source.
Every configured calendar signal traces to a captured working request and is revisited when the captures change.
SchoolMessenger calendar event data is out of reach by policy rather than merely unbuilt.
Existing Landing associations are migration inputs and become package facts only when they contain confirmed stable references.
Landing SyncRun step trees are source-backed opaque checkpoints rather than universal connector lifecycle semantics.
Hosts schedule eligible retries, while Aleph owns transition and retry-eligibility semantics.
A domain-run migration reconciler supplies stable provider-account and domain references instead of promoting Landing foreign keys or labels.
Hosts authenticate callers and evaluate manual-launch policy before supplying Aleph with stable actor and authorization-decision references.
Queue adapters enforce the concurrency and rate policy supplied by Aleph and may prune their own transport records without affecting attempt observability.
Connectors own opaque checkpoint serialization; monotonic checkpoints additionally expose a comparable non-negative position.

decisions.decision: Implement only the web.crawl capability from ALEPH-001.
decisions.rationale: No second executable connector yet justifies generic manifest, checkpoint, approval, or parallel-work contracts.

decisions.decision: Require Funes acceptance before a frontier candidate becomes fetched.
decisions.rationale: Operational success must not precede canonical content persistence.

decisions.decision: Resume interrupted Funes submissions in the same ingestion run.
decisions.rationale: Funes acceptance is idempotent and a stranded fetching candidate can be returned to pending safely.

decisions.decision: Record external URLs in both operational frontier evidence and Funes discovery provenance.
decisions.rationale: Their existence and parent relationship matter even though they are outside the recursive crawl boundary.

decisions.decision: Select one versioned extractor from the normalized response media type.
decisions.rationale: Classification and derivation remain deterministic, queryable, and replayable against preserved bytes.

decisions.decision: Preserve link, iframe, and embed as distinct discovery relationships.
decisions.rationale: How an artifact is connected to its parent is part of the provenance proof.

decisions.decision: Use smalot/pdfparser only inside aleph.pdf:1.
decisions.rationale: Reliable PDF text extraction exceeds the safe scope of an in-package parser and the single call site bounds removal cost.

decisions.decision: Use landing's names for database concepts shared with Aleph.
decisions.rationale: The master schema must retain every landing table and column while package migrations add only new prefixed tables; ingestion-run outcomes therefore use stats and error.

decisions.decision: Take shared column names from the landing model-attribute ownership matrix.
decisions.rationale: D-016 states the principle and the matrix resolves it case by case; fetched_at was a package-local synonym for observed_at and the new columns are payload_hash, byte_size, and ingested_at.

decisions.decision: Record on the frontier row what the Funes acceptance boundary returned rather than reading Funes tables or recomputing hashes.
decisions.rationale: The inventory needs hashes, sizes, and extraction status without crossing the boundary D-002 established or creating a second authority for the same value.

decisions.decision: Configure calendar-like classification per source instead of compiling vendor URL shapes into Aleph.
decisions.rationale: ALEPH-011 admits only captured working requests as evidence, and the capture disproved the recalled platform route convention.

decisions.decision: Mark a resource calendar-like by path or by one level of iframe or embed parentage.
decisions.rationale: The Waverly artifact is a Google Drive URL that is calendrical only because of the edge reaching it.

decisions.decision: Separate current, stale, and unobserved rows in the inventory.
decisions.rationale: A page-limited or interrupted run leaves candidates whose content is known but not current, which is the distinction an operator is asking about.

decisions.decision: Make the inventory deterministic by fixed columns, PHP-side canonical-URL ordering, UTC instants, and no generation timestamp.
decisions.rationale: Reproducibility must be a testable property, and two exports must be diffable.

decisions.decision: Treat an empty response body as an empty document in aleph.html:1.
decisions.rationale: A body-less 404 was recorded as a failed extraction, which claims the extractor broke; the version has never shipped, so it is fixed in place rather than as aleph.html:2.

decisions.decision: Store the prefixed source reference web:ahsd in aleph_ingestion_runs.source_reference so it matches funes_sources.reference exactly.
decisions.rationale: Joining an Aleph run to its Funes source should be an equality, not an equality plus a prefixing rule living in application code; landing offers no competing convention because its sync-run tables identify a source by foreign key.

decisions.decision: Represent source scopes with typed namespaced opaque references and explicit confirmed, ambiguous, rejected, or superseded state.
decisions.rationale: Host database IDs, display names, and path inference are not portable facts; multiple rows preserve many-to-many truth and ambiguity without guessing.

decisions.decision: Evolve the existing Aleph ingestion run into the portable SyncRun object while preserving Landing's repository step tree as an opaque checkpoint.
decisions.rationale: A second package run model would split lifecycle authority, and copying a GitHub-specific UI model would force accidental complexity onto every connector.

decisions.decision: Represent queue retries as numbered durable attempts inside one idempotent ingestion run and expose them through a stable query read model.
decisions.rationale: One run identity preserves source-window lineage and accepted-history deduplication, while durable attempts retain the operational evidence a queue worker cannot.

decisions.decision: Represent DomainSyncRun as a typed DNS projection over the shared ingestion run, with source-backed DNS fields isolated under one extension.
decisions.rationale: Landing adds DNS scope to the same lifecycle, so a second lifecycle would duplicate rules and provider SDK objects would leak implementation detail.

decisions.decision: Persist or resolve an authorized idempotent manual run before handing it to a host-owned dispatch port.
decisions.rationale: Every entry adapter needs identical lifecycle semantics, while authentication, UI, and queue transport are genuine host integration boundaries.

decisions.decision: Project universal envelope data and each connector extension into separate versioned Funes metadata assertions.
decisions.rationale: The Funes boundary now preserves namespace, schema version, provenance, and assertion time; rebuilding the legacy nested JSON slot would discard those semantics and duplicate its metadata model.

decisions.decision: Create a durable pending ingestion attempt before dispatching a runtime-neutral queued unit.
decisions.rationale: Queue tables are disposable transport state; the existing numbered attempt is the smallest durable place for queue class, priority, tags, policy, heartbeat, worker identity, failure, and retry lineage.

decisions.decision: Store checkpoints as append-only accepted-through commits keyed by stream, capability, and partition.
decisions.rationale: Opaque run JSON cannot detect competing writers, isolate partitions, preserve serializer evolution, or prove which Funes observations were safe before a cursor advanced.

decisions.decision: Record incomplete outcomes and their safe recovery action in the package read model.
decisions.rationale: Domain failures, queue failures, cancellations, rate limits, and blocked credentials require distinct recovery even after host queue records are pruned.

decisions.decision: Retry by creating one idempotent child attempt from durable run state.
decisions.rationale: Queue payloads are mutable transport records; retry lineage and accepted-through checkpoints must remain authoritative after those records are pruned.

decisions.decision: Resume leased partitions from accepted-through checkpoints under explicit work budgets.
decisions.rationale: An interrupted worker payload may be ahead of durable acceptance; bounded replay is safer than missing accepted records.

decisions.decision: Project source-stream timestamps durably while deriving current freshness from an explicit clock.
decisions.rationale: A stored healthy label ages without writes, while host-side derivation would split semantics across CLI, API, mobile, and desktop clients.

decisions.decision: Represent connector health as latest expiring evidence per dimension with coded remediation.
decisions.rationale: A universal boolean hides the difference between bad credentials, provider reachability, rate state, stale data, queue backlog, and missing evidence.

decisions.decision: Persist recurring cadence and dispatch identity in Aleph while leaving scheduler wakeups to the host.
decisions.rationale: Provider-specific host commands duplicate cadence rules, and two scheduler processes need one durable lock and occurrence identity.

decisions.decision: Represent historical imports as idempotent bounded runs with deterministic durable partitions.
decisions.rationale: Provider-specific commands and queue payloads cannot provide one auditable pause, resume, progress, and completion contract.

decisions.decision: Advance incremental checkpoints only through idempotent Funes-accepted material changes.
decisions.rationale: Provider cursors and timestamps alone cannot prove edits or deletions reached durable history, and unchanged polls must not invent accepted work.

decisions.decision: Use one source installation as the isolation boundary for each provider account and keep managed credentials in encrypted referenced rows.
decisions.rationale: Provider-wide configuration collides across accounts, while Funes identity must not carry rotating secrets and provider-specific account tables would duplicate operational scoping.

decisions.decision: Enforce the Aleph package boundary with an executable end-to-end connector gate and structural dependency checks.
decisions.rationale: Architecture prose and live-provider smoke tests cannot prove that Funes remains discovery-free, provider SDKs remain outside the core, or replay preserves one accepted historical effect.

decisions.decision: Observe Git as SHA-addressed repository, ref movement, commit, tree, file, change, diff, and blame facts behind a replaceable source contract.
decisions.rationale: A current-file projection erases deletions and force-pushes, while local paths, GitHub payloads, and symbol interpretation do not belong in the portable observation contract.

decisions.decision: Import Landing GitHub runs as deterministic shared ingestion runs with GitHub-only scope in an extension projection.
decisions.rationale: Status, timing, retry, checkpoint, progress, and failure behavior are provider-neutral, while repository watches, targets, and reconciliation IDs must remain operational rather than historical payloads.

decisions.decision: Use one canonical GitHub activity identity for polling and webhook transports.
decisions.rationale: Repository coordinates, node ID, update time, and canonical payload describe provider history; cursor, delivery, and transport details are operational provenance that must not duplicate the same change.

decisions.decision: Model repository watches as portable orchestration state with per-watch trigger coalescing.
decisions.rationale: Cadence, checkpoint, enablement, due time, error, and backoff decide when ingestion runs, while provider history belongs in Funes and transport-specific payloads belong behind adapters.

decisions.decision: Route repository watch signals through existing incremental-run identity using watch, ref, and head.
decisions.rationale: This coalesces polling and webhooks without duplicating lifecycle machinery, lets polling repair missed webhooks, and prevents a watch head from advancing before accepted checkpoint completion.

decisions.decision: Apply deterministic shell secret redaction before constructing immutable Funes envelopes.
decisions.rationale: Commands and output commonly contain credentials, and an immutable acceptance boundary is too late to remove them; source revision and host/user context provide replay-safe identity without retaining raw adapter metadata.

decisions.decision: Retain provider-specific AI records and blocks inside a neutral message graph.
decisions.rationale: Common roles, authors, chronology, and parent links support cross-provider queries, while untouched provider evidence preserves tool linkage and fields that do not justify universal schema.

decisions.decision: Model LinearSyncRun as a typed Linear projection over the shared ingestion-run lifecycle.
decisions.rationale: Status, timing, retry, failure, counters, checkpoints, and accepted history are already shared semantics; only workspace/project scope and provider reconciliation belong in the Linear extension.

decisions.decision: Checkpoint Linear resource streams independently and converge polling and webhooks before Funes acceptance.
decisions.rationale: Projects, issues, and updates paginate independently, transport overlap must not duplicate provider history, and attachment provenance does not justify an Aleph artifact store.

decisions.decision: Normalize Gmail, Microsoft Graph, and IMAP to F28 before history and checkpoint each bounded page after acceptance.
decisions.rationale: Original transport evidence must survive without SDK or credential leakage, participant resolution requires an external authority, and advancing provider state before Funes acceptance can skip mail permanently.

decisions.decision: Represent Slack tokens as portable status metadata plus an opaque host secret-store reference.
decisions.rationale: Connector orchestration needs workspace, scopes, availability, and lifecycle state but not token material; legacy ciphertext must remain until a host proves secure live cutover.

decisions.decision: Model SlackSyncRun as a typed Slack projection over the shared ingestion-run lifecycle.
decisions.rationale: Landing repeats shared run status/timing/counter/failure behavior, while workspace/channel scope and reconciled continuation state are the only Slack-specific operational facts.

decisions.decision: Converge Slack polling and Events API before Funes and checkpoint cursor/high-water only after acceptance.
decisions.rationale: Transport overlap must not duplicate messages, incomplete paging must retain its cursor without advancing the floor, and attachment bytes belong to downstream owners.

open_questions: Should frontier identity collapse distinct requested URLs that resolve to the same canonical final URL?
Which AHSD query parameters demonstrate stable resource identity strongly enough to enter the allowlist?
When does measured crawl throughput justify concurrency greater than one?
Should district PDFs keep the CDN final URL as their Funes identity, or should the pre-redirect allowed-host URL be recorded instead?
When does inventory size justify a payload-free existence read on ObservationStore instead of find()?
Which authority will issue canonical project references when several stable namespaces describe the same project?
Which stable connector installation should each provider-specific Landing run family reference during migration?
Should provider retry timing remain entirely host-scheduled, or will two consumers demonstrate timing semantics that belong in Aleph?
Which source-backed DNS provider reconciliation identifiers should each connector retain long term?
Will a demonstrated host require authorization expiry or policy-version evidence beyond actor and decision references?
Which connectors demonstrate stable queue priority, concurrency, or rate budgets that should override the per-installation defaults?
Which Landing timestamp and cursor fields can be retired after each connector reconciles its active stream checkpoint history?
constraints: Only public GET and HEAD retrievals are permitted.
Page count, depth, timeouts, redirects, response size, retries, and host rate are bounded.
External URLs must never be recursively crawled.
Aleph must not become a second canonical content store.
A run cannot complete while required Funes acceptance has failed.
SchoolMessenger may be investigated only through captured working requests; no endpoint may be constructed from identifiers found in markup.
The inventory derives on read and adds no store.
The same crawl state must export byte-identical JSON and CSV.
Package tables may add columns, but may not introduce a name the master schema already spells differently.
An inventory may only be produced for a run belonging to the named source.
A source scope may not use an unqualified display name or host database integer as a cross-package identity.
Ambiguous associations must remain explicit and must not be promoted by name similarity.
Historical records stay in Funes; ingestion runs may retain only stable accepted-history references.
Landing sync-run persistence remains until cutover reconciliation passes.
Funes owns accepted historical observations; Aleph attempts retain only their stable references.
Manual launch must persist or resolve its run before dispatch and must never dispatch an identical request twice.

glossary.capability: A declared provider-neutral connector operation; web.crawl is the first with a complete executable package pipeline.
glossary.ingestion_run: One idempotent logical execution of a capability for a connector source, containing one or more attempts.
glossary.frontier: The retained operational set of pending, fetching, fetched, failed, and skipped canonical URLs.
glossary.observation: An immutable Funes content record created or reused for a retrieved response.
glossary.disposition: Funes' first, unchanged, or changed classification for accepted content.
glossary.mechanical_extraction: A versioned HTML, PDF, or unsupported derivation recorded against one immutable Funes observation.
glossary.discovery_relationship: A link, iframe, or embed edge from an observed parent resource to a canonical discovered resource.
glossary.inventory: A deterministic report of one ingestion run: bounds, totals, and one row per frontier candidate joined to what Funes returned.
glossary.crawl_bounds: The limits and policy a run actually applied, read back from its recorded parameters.
glossary.freshness: Whether a row's content evidence is current, stale, or unobserved.
glossary.calendar_signal: Why a resource is calendar-like: path or embedded_in_calendar.
glossary.external_embed: An inventory row outside the allowed hosts whose discovery origin is iframe or embed.
glossary.source_reference: The prefixed identity of a source, web:<key>, spelled identically in aleph_ingestion_runs and funes_sources.
glossary.extraction_status: The typed outcome of one mechanical extraction: succeeded or failed.
glossary.entity_reference: A typed namespaced opaque Funes reference for a project, identity, repository, organization, or domain.
glossary.source_scope_association: A state-bearing relation from a source installation or stream to an entity reference.
glossary.domain_reconciliation: An actor-and-time decision relating an observed domain stream to stable project, site, or repository references.
glossary.run_completeness: Whether a run observed all, some, or not-yet-all of its requested source range.
glossary.legacy_run_reference: A namespaced stable identity retained from an application-owned run before package migration.
glossary.ingestion_attempt: One numbered execution inside a logical ingestion run, carrying its checkpoint, counters, failure, and timing.
glossary.run_read_model: A presentation-neutral projection of a run, its attempts, diagnostics, and next safe action.
glossary.recovery_action: The machine-readable safe next step for an ingestion run.
glossary.retry_lineage: The durable parent-child link between a failed or partial attempt and its idempotent retry.
glossary.ingestion_continuation: The latest accepted-through checkpoint used to reconstruct one partition after interruption.
glossary.continuation_lease: An expiring exclusive claim on one stream capability partition during resume.
glossary.source_stream_freshness: The last-attempt, last-success, accepted-through, next-due, and current freshness projection for one stream.
glossary.freshness_expectation: The expected interval and stale boundary applied by the package freshness query.
glossary.connector_health_check: An expiring immutable result for one installation health dimension.
glossary.health_remediation: A coded plain-language next step attached to a health result.
glossary.ingestion_schedule: A recurring supported capability for one source installation with cron cadence, timezone, constraints, and next due time.
glossary.schedule_dispatch: The immutable association between one schedule occurrence and its ingestion run.
glossary.backfill_range: Two connector-owned boundary values and their explicit format for a bounded historical import.
glossary.ingestion_partition: One ordered durable slice of a backfill run with checkpoint, counters, and lifecycle.
glossary.incremental_strategy: Cursor, high-water, webhook, hash, or reconcile semantics declared by one source stream.
glossary.incremental_change: One idempotent Funes-accepted added, updated, or deleted provider event.
glossary.source_account: One independently enabled connector installation with provider and Funes account identities.
glossary.connector_credential: Encrypted account-specific authentication material addressed by an opaque reference with scopes, expiry, and refresh metadata.
glossary.git_repository_source: A replaceable reader that returns stable repository identity and captured ref snapshots.
glossary.git_ref_movement: A previous-SHA to head-SHA observation that explicitly records broken ancestry.
glossary.git_file_change: An added, modified, deleted, or renamed path derived from previous and current trees.
glossary.github_ingestion_run: A shared ingestion run projected with GitHub account, repository, watch, target, reconciliation, and scope metadata.
glossary.github_activity: A canonical GitHub node revision shared by poll and webhook observation paths.
glossary.github_webhook_delivery: A signature-verified encrypted payload unique by source installation and delivery ID, retaining accepted history references for replay.
glossary.repository_watch: Portable poll, webhook, or hybrid orchestration state for one installation and stable repository reference.
glossary.repository_watch_trigger: A stable per-watch change identity that coalesces duplicate provider observations before work is launched.
glossary.repository_watch_signal: A provider-neutral poll, webhook, or reconciliation observation naming one repository ref and head.
glossary.shell_command_observation: A human or agent command with stable source revision and complete host/user execution context.
glossary.shell_redaction_decision: A retained or redacted pre-acceptance outcome carrying policy identity, reasons, and original command hash.
glossary.ai_conversation: One provider session with a stable provider ID, source revision, raw reference, metadata, and ordered neutral message graph.
glossary.ai_message_part: One ordered neutral content part that retains its raw provider block and optional tool-call linkage.
glossary.linear_ingestion_run: A shared ingestion run projected with Linear workspace/project scope, provider run and reconciliation IDs, targets, and per-stream cursors.
glossary.linear_activity: A canonical Linear resource revision identified by workspace, kind, provider ID, source timestamp, and provider payload.
glossary.linear_stream_checkpoint: An accepted-through cursor isolated to one independently paginated Linear workspace stream.
glossary.f28_email_message: A provider-neutral email revision retaining provider and RFC identity, threading, original source values, normalized fields, mailbox state, attachment references, and provenance.
glossary.email_provider_checkpoint: An opaque Gmail history ID, Graph delta link, or IMAP UID state committed after Funes acceptance.
glossary.digory_attachment_handoff: A stable reference to provider-owned attachment content that Aleph does not retrieve or store.
glossary.slack_credential_handle: Workspace-scoped metadata and an opaque reference resolved only by a host secret store.
glossary.slack_credential_state: The active, expired, revoked, or missing availability of one Slack workspace credential.
glossary.slack_ingestion_run: A shared ingestion run projected with Slack workspace/channel scope, provider references, targets, and continuation checkpoint.
glossary.slack_activity: A canonical workspace, user, channel, message, file, or link revision shared across polling and Events API.
glossary.slack_cursor_high_water_checkpoint: An accepted-through partition value carrying continuation cursor and high-water timestamp.
glossary.domain_ingestion_run: A DNS-specific projection that adds stable account/domain scope and provider reconciliation references to the shared ingestion run.
glossary.manual_launch: An authorized idempotent request that persists a pending run before host dispatch.
glossary.authorization_decision_reference: A stable host-issued reference to the evaluated decision that allowed a manual run.
